explanation: The prior document (2018-12-19) delivered a hawkish surprise: the Fed hiked rates to 2.25-2.5% while signaling 'some further gradual increases,' with the SEP still projecting two more hikes in 2019, which markets interpreted as insufficiently sensitive to tightening financial conditions and global growth risks. The subsequent document (2019-01-30) explicitly confirms this, noting that 'market participants appeared to interpret FOMC communications at the time of the December meeting as not fully appreciating the tightening of financial conditions' and that investors perceived the FOMC as 'insufficiently flexible'—directly linking the December 19 communication to the late-December market deterioration that would encompass the 2018-12-28 structural break date.
